prospect.name: Darius Knox
prospect.location: Currently in Thailand, considering permanent relocation; originally United States
prospect.occupation: Retired from the United States Marine Corps since about 2019, on a pension plus disability pay. Cybersecurity engineer by trade, not currently working in it. Recently ran a small trucking business with several trucks and hired drivers, since sold and liquidated.
prospect.training_background: Trained before and during Marine Corps service. Strong on pull-ups and bodyweight work. Some kettlebell experience with a 30 lb bell at home, knows goblet squats, working on snatch technique. Plays basketball and says he still moves like he did in his twenties. Walks 7,000-10,000 steps a day. Current training is sporadic and self-directed — push-ups and squats as the mood takes him. Has watched Trevor's YouTube content for a long time.
prospect.medical: Explicitly denied injuries and health conditions when asked: 'No injuries and anything like that. No health issues.' Reports increasing joint pain when lifting barbells and dumbbells that does not appear with kettlebells, and long-standing hip and hip-flexor tightness he has had essentially always — cannot sit cross-legged comfortably and is stiff getting up off the floor. Receives US military disability pay, the basis of which was not discussed. Mentioned developing a mild fever during the call, which he described as fine and attributed with the rep to air conditioning.

signals: Zero price resistance at any point — heard $6,000, asked only how it was structured, and paid within minutes: 'I mean, it sounds good.'
Financially settled and unpressured: military pension plus disability, sold a trucking business, on an extended stay in Thailand deciding whether to relocate permanently

Explicitly good-to-great in his own words: 'my physique has always been like average, sometimes above average, but you don't want to get it dialed in. I just want to get it dialed in where I know how to keep it that way. Instead of it always being fluctuating.'

Buying structure rather than rescue: 'I just really need structure... a structured program, something kind of tailored to me specifically opposed to, like, finding a workout online, just cookie-cutting to everybody'

Partial overlap with the_preserver on his stated why — 'preventive maintenance... making sure that I can get out of the chair without having to put my hands' — but he has ample discretionary liquidity and also wants to gain, so the optimizer read is primary

goals.text: Get a structured, tailored programme instead of winging it and getting bored
Improve mobility — he is stiff, especially in the hips and hip flexors, and cannot sit cross-legged comfortably
Build core strength, which he considers weak
Build functional strength rather than robotic barbell and dumbbell movements that hurt his joints in his forties
Better body composition and more muscle mass, evenly distributed
Master kettlebell technique, including cleaning the snatch without banging his wrists
Preventive maintenance so that later in life he can still get out of a chair without using his hands and get up off the floor
A training method that travels with him as a digital nomad without needing a gym membership

pains.text: No structure — wings his workouts, gets bored, then cycles in and out of training
Stiff hips and hip flexors he has had essentially all his life; uncomfortable sitting cross-legged or rising from the floor
Joint pain that builds up when training with barbells and dumbbells and does not occur with kettlebells
Bored by traditional gym training and the robotic movement patterns it involves
Uneven development he cannot correct alone — rear delts flat, inner chest lagging
Constant travel and an unsettled living situation between Thailand and the United States
Fluctuating physique he has never managed to hold steady

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep stated most clients pay upfront by credit card, then recommended the interest-free half-split as the better option: '$3K now and $3K in 30 days', explicitly 'there's no interest on it'. A monthly plan was raised by the prospect's own arithmetic and the rep began to note it carries a cost before the prospect waved it off. The prospect took the half-split and paid the first $3,000 on the call. Total contract value is $6,000 with no surcharge — the only clean pricing in this batch.

evidence: Payment link sent in chat, card details entered live and payment confirmed: 'I think I sent the payment on, yeah, and showed me that, oh yeah, yeah, it went through, yeah, it went through.'
Onboarding call with Trevor agreed for Tuesday the 30th at midnight Thailand time, the prospect choosing that over the 5.15am alternative.
Confirmation emails received and read back by the prospect: 'I see the one about the appointment here, and let me see about, okay, welcome to kettlebell body.'
Email and phone confirmed on the call for the account record.

Counter-evidence: only the first $3,000 of $6,000 has been collected, with the balance due in 30 days; the agreement was not signed on the call but deferred to a laptop; and no Skool community link was mentioned at all, unlike the other close in this batch.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor Tuesday the 30th at midnight Thailand time. Prospect to sign the agreement on a laptop and complete the onboarding form before that call. Second $3,000 instalment due in 30 days.

notable.note: The rep tried to disqualify this prospect three minutes in — 'I don't want to waste your time. I think this is not the right solution for you, because from what I'm hearing, you're looking more into bodybuilding type of stuff that you want to precisely correct some composition of the body. And kettlebells don't work like that' — and the prospect responded by restating his goals to fit the product: 'Maybe I was just talking about other goals that had nothing to do with kettlebell.' The original goal (even muscle distribution, rear delts, inner chest) was never revisited, so a stated primary objective the rep had declared out of scope went into a closed deal unresolved. Separately, the rep used his own medical history as proof: he says he was born with genetic hip degeneration, that doctors told him fifteen years ago to have surgery as soon as possible, and that he is still mobile 'thanks to kettlebells'. Pricing on this call was the only clean pricing in the batch — $6,000 for six months, split interest-free into two $3,000 payments, no invented tier and no surcharge.

quality.notes: Two structural problems. First, roughly seven and a half minutes are missing from the recording: the transcript jumps from 00:06:35 to 00:14:00, where the prospect says 'Hello. All right, we're back. Oh, yeah, I tried to do a hotspot to my laptop.' The rep's injuries question at 00:06:35 had to be repeated after the gap. Second, the prospect's speaker label changes mid-call from 'Darius Knox' to lowercase 'darius' at that same point, when he rejoined from a different device — same person, recorded as aka. Beyond that, inversion is extensive: at 00:20:09-00:20:24 'How old are you exactly?' and '45' are both labelled to the rep and the prospect alternately in a way that makes the ages read backwards, though content resolves it (prospect 45, rep 43). The pricing exchange at 00:33:20 attributes 'the investment is 6K' to the prospect. Roles read from content throughout.
